_metadata._caveat: All clinical, surveillance, and household data is fully synthetic. No real PHI. EPA EQI values approximated. ADHS/CDC magnitudes calibrated to public reports.

counties._description: Arizona county reference data. FIPS codes are real (US Census). EPA EQI values are approximated from Lobdell et al. 2014 county-level composites (negative = better quality, positive = worse). Coccidioides endemicity ratings are derived from CDC/ADHS surveillance data.

_source_notes.epa_eqi: Approximated from EPA EQI 2006-2010 county dataset

terminologies._description: Clinical terminologies for the ONE-HealthRecord MVP demo. Includes Arizona-relevant zoonotic diseases plus chronic conditions for longitudinal records.

_sources.snomed_vet: Virginia-Maryland College of Vet Medicine SNOMED-CT Veterinary Extension

_metadata._phase: Phase 5 — ZIP-resolution dataset expansion (200% scale, 14 One Health diseases, transmission-route-aware)

households.name: Hernandez
households.narrative: Hernandez household, Tucson (Pima Co.). Maria (52) was diagnosed with coccidioidomycosis 14 days ago. Family dog Rocco was diagnosed by their veterinarian 6 days ago with the same organism. Husband Carlos (54) presented today with a 3-week cough not yet worked up.

households.name: Johnson
households.narrative: Johnson household, Florence (Pinal Co.). Dog Bella was diagnosed with ehrlichiosis 8 days ago. Tom (47) was bitten by a tick and presents today with fever, headache, and developing maculopapular rash.

households.name: Williams

animal_reporting._note: Not formally reportable for animals, but ADHS encourages cross-species sentinel notification given AZ endemicity.

households.narrative: Williams household, rural Maricopa Co. Couple (Robert 68, Linda 65) with rodent infestation in detached garage that they cleaned out 10 days ago. Robert presents today with fever, myalgia, and progressive dyspnea. HPS must be flagged.

households.name: Patel
households.narrative: Patel household, Yuma. Dog Rex was diagnosed with leptospirosis 3 days ago after swimming in an irrigation canal where the family also swims. Prophylactic alert recommended.

households.name: Chen
households.narrative: Chen household, Flagstaff. Healthy young family. Negative control.

households.name: Begay
households.narrative: Begay household, near St. Johns (Apache Co.). Outdoor cat Shadow caught and consumed multiple ground squirrels in the past month. Cat presented to vet 4 days ago with high fever and lymphadenopathy — diagnosed plague. Now Sarah Begay (38) presents today with fever, painful inguinal lymph node, and rapid decline. Plague is a Class A reportable disease.

households.name: Ramirez
households.narrative: Ramirez household, near Bisbee (Cochise Co.). Owns small horse stable. Horse Trigger developed ataxia and weakness 12 days ago — vet confirmed WNV. Standing water on property after monsoon rains. Today, Roberto Ramirez (59) presents with severe headache, fever, and confusion. Suspect West Nile encephalitis — both share the mosquito vector exposure.

households.name: Thompson
households.narrative: Thompson household, near Kingman (Mohave Co.). Dog Buddy was attacked by a skunk in the yard 6 days ago — skunk tested positive for rabies. Dog is currently in 45-day strict observation. Today, son Jake (12) presents with a small unhealed wound on his hand from breaking up the encounter. Post-exposure prophylaxis indicated.

households.name: Becker
households.narrative: Becker family, small goat dairy near Patagonia (Santa Cruz Co.). Three goats had spontaneous abortions over the past 3 weeks — Coxiella burnetii confirmed. James Becker (44) presents today with 2 weeks of dry cough, fever, and fatigue. Q fever should be on the differential given direct exposure to placental tissue during goat birthing.

households.name: Nguyen
households.narrative: Nguyen household, central Phoenix. Pet parrot Mango has been listless and fluffed-up for 2 weeks; vet confirmed Chlamydia psittaci. Today, Lan Nguyen (34) presents with 5 days of high fever, dry cough, and severe headache. Atypical pneumonia with bird exposure → psittacosis must be considered.

households.name: Sanchez
households.narrative: Sanchez household, near Florence (Pinal Co.). Carlos Sanchez (51) is an avid hunter; field-dressed wild rabbits 8 days ago without gloves after noting one rabbit appeared sick. Now presents with fever, painful axillary lymph node, and a non-healing skin ulcer at the field-dressing site. Tularemia (ulceroglandular form) highly suspected.

households.name: Yazzie
households.narrative: Yazzie household, near Holbrook (Navajo Co.). Pet bearded dragon Spike. Daughter Ellie (5) presents today with 4 days of severe diarrhea, fever, and dehydration. Salmonella isolated from stool. Pet reptile is a well-known reservoir; child handles Spike daily.

nodes.name: Hernandez
nodes.narrative: Hernandez household, Tucson (Pima Co.). Maria (52) was diagnosed with coccidioidomycosis 14 days ago. Family dog Rocco was diagnosed by their veterinarian 6 days ago with the same organism. Husband Carlos (54) presented today with a 3-week cough not yet worked up.
nodes.label: Hernandez household

nodes.name: Johnson
nodes.narrative: Johnson household, Florence (Pinal Co.). Dog Bella was diagnosed with ehrlichiosis 8 days ago. Tom (47) was bitten by a tick and presents today with fever, headache, and developing maculopapular rash.
nodes.label: Johnson household

nodes.name: Williams
nodes.narrative: Williams household, rural Maricopa Co. Couple (Robert 68, Linda 65) with rodent infestation in detached garage that they cleaned out 10 days ago. Robert presents today with fever, myalgia, and progressive dyspnea. HPS must be flagged.
nodes.label: Williams household

nodes.name: Patel
nodes.narrative: Patel household, Yuma. Dog Rex was diagnosed with leptospirosis 3 days ago after swimming in an irrigation canal where the family also swims. Prophylactic alert recommended.
nodes.label: Patel household

nodes.name: Chen
nodes.narrative: Chen household, Flagstaff. Healthy young family. Negative control.
nodes.label: Chen household

nodes.name: Begay
nodes.narrative: Begay household, near St. Johns (Apache Co.). Outdoor cat Shadow caught and consumed multiple ground squirrels in the past month. Cat presented to vet 4 days ago with high fever and lymphadenopathy — diagnosed plague. Now Sarah Begay (38) presents today with fever, painful inguinal lymph node, and rapid decline. Plague is a Class A reportable disease.
nodes.label: Begay household

nodes.name: Ramirez
nodes.narrative: Ramirez household, near Bisbee (Cochise Co.). Owns small horse stable. Horse Trigger developed ataxia and weakness 12 days ago — vet confirmed WNV. Standing water on property after monsoon rains. Today, Roberto Ramirez (59) presents with severe headache, fever, and confusion. Suspect West Nile encephalitis — both share the mosquito vector exposure.
nodes.label: Ramirez household

nodes.name: Thompson
nodes.narrative: Thompson household, near Kingman (Mohave Co.). Dog Buddy was attacked by a skunk in the yard 6 days ago — skunk tested positive for rabies. Dog is currently in 45-day strict observation. Today, son Jake (12) presents with a small unhealed wound on his hand from breaking up the encounter. Post-exposure prophylaxis indicated.
nodes.label: Thompson household

nodes.name: Becker
nodes.narrative: Becker family, small goat dairy near Patagonia (Santa Cruz Co.). Three goats had spontaneous abortions over the past 3 weeks — Coxiella burnetii confirmed. James Becker (44) presents today with 2 weeks of dry cough, fever, and fatigue. Q fever should be on the differential given direct exposure to placental tissue during goat birthing.
nodes.label: Becker household

nodes.name: Nguyen
nodes.narrative: Nguyen household, central Phoenix. Pet parrot Mango has been listless and fluffed-up for 2 weeks; vet confirmed Chlamydia psittaci. Today, Lan Nguyen (34) presents with 5 days of high fever, dry cough, and severe headache. Atypical pneumonia with bird exposure → psittacosis must be considered.
nodes.label: Nguyen household

nodes.name: Sanchez
nodes.narrative: Sanchez household, near Florence (Pinal Co.). Carlos Sanchez (51) is an avid hunter; field-dressed wild rabbits 8 days ago without gloves after noting one rabbit appeared sick. Now presents with fever, painful axillary lymph node, and a non-healing skin ulcer at the field-dressing site. Tularemia (ulceroglandular form) highly suspected.
nodes.label: Sanchez household

nodes.name: Yazzie
nodes.narrative: Yazzie household, near Holbrook (Navajo Co.). Pet bearded dragon Spike. Daughter Ellie (5) presents today with 4 days of severe diarrhea, fever, and dehydration. Salmonella isolated from stool. Pet reptile is a well-known reservoir; child handles Spike daily.
nodes.label: Yazzie household

alerts.title: Vector anomaly — Pinal County tick burden
alerts.summary: Tick collection counts 26.2σ above baseline in Pinal Co. (last 4 weeks vs. trailing 22)
alerts.rationale: Mean tick count in Pinal County over the past 4 weeks (924/trap) is 26.2 standard deviations above the trailing-22-week baseline (108±31). Predominant species: Rhipicephalus sanguineus. Elevated risk for tick-borne diseases including ehrlichiosis and RMSF — consider clinician advisory for the county.

federation_manifest._description: Federation manifest. Maps every patient and every household to the site that owns the primary record. The ONE-HealthRecord application uses this manifest to compose cross-site FHIR queries — it does NOT hold primary clinical data itself.
federation_manifest._caveat: Synthetic. Production: this manifest is itself a federated structure — each site publishes its own /Patient catalog, and an enterprise Master Patient Index (eMPI) reconciles identities across sites.

consents._description: Cross-species linkage consent records, household-level. Each record encodes whether the household has authorized the system to publish cross-species linkage signals (the One Health pointer that connects human and animal records in the same household). Consent is REQUIRED for cross-species linkage. It is NOT required for individual clinical care or for aggregate public-health surveillance — those continue regardless.
consents._caveat: Synthetic. In production: consent is captured at intake on the OHR-CONSENT-01 form (paper or e-signature), with explicit language reviewed by the local IRB. Tribal-land households follow the local tribal IRB's consent template, not the default form. Consent can be revoked at any time; revocation immediately suppresses the cross-species pointer.

empi_links._description: Probabilistic record linkage results. Pairs are scored on five fields (last_name, first_name, dob, address, zip) using a Fellegi-Sunter weighted log-likelihood. Tiers: auto_link (p ≥ 0.95) → linked automatically; clerical_review (0.80 ≤ p < 0.95) → queued for human reviewer; no_match (p < 0.80) → ignored.
empi_links._caveat: Synthetic. Production uses Splink (open-source) or commercial eMPIs (NextGate, Verato). Animal-owner reconciliation is harder than human reconciliation because no national owner-identifier exists; we approximate by treating the owner's name + DOB + address as the matching key.

_metadata.title: U.S. Reportable Diseases Database — Arizona-First with Federal Cross-Reference
_metadata.scope: Every disease on the ADHS R9-6-202 list, cross-referenced against CDC NNDSS, USDA APHIS NLRAD, AZ Department of Agriculture, and AZ Game and Fish where applicable.

sources.doc: Arizona Administrative Code R9-6-202 — Reportable Diseases List
National Notifiable Diseases Surveillance System (NNDSS) Conditions
National List of Reportable Animal Diseases (NLRAD) / NAHRS Reportable Disease List
Arizona Administrative Code R3-2-402 — Mandatory Disease Reporting by Veterinarians and Veterinary Laboratories
Veterinarian Reporting Requirements — Required & Recommended Reportable Zoonotic Diseases in Arizona

_metadata._caveat: Compiled from public sources; intended for the ONE-HealthRecord MVP. Production deployment must keep this database in sync with the live ADHS / CDC / APHIS lists, which update annually. Consider sourcing via API rather than static file in production.

timeline_legend.immediate: Submit through electronic reporting system or by telephone within 24 hours after a case or suspect case is diagnosed, treated, or detected (ADHS lightning bolt symbol)
timeline_legend.one_working_day: Submit within one working day through electronic reporting system or by telephone after a case or suspect case is diagnosed, treated, or detected (ADHS exclamation mark symbol)
timeline_legend.five_working_days: Submit within five working days after a case or suspect case is diagnosed, treated, or detected (ADHS computer/monitor symbol)
timeline_legend.outbreak_24h: Submit within 24 hours after detecting an outbreak (ADHS circle symbol)
timeline_legend.monitored_30d: Monitored disease — report within 30 days (USDA NLRAD)
timeline_legend.notifiable_24h: Notifiable disease — report within 24 hours (USDA NLRAD)

diseases._note: Reportable as an outbreak signal; individual sporadic cases are not.

animal_reporting._note: Eastern, Western, Venezuelan equine encephalomyelitis is required-reportable for veterinarians (ADA).

diseases.common_name: HIV infection and related disease in an infant

animal_reporting._note: ADA + ADHS dual reporting required for veterinary cases.
AGFD/ADHS recommended for animal cases (especially feline plague — cats can transmit to humans).

diseases.common_name: Rabies in an animal (confirmed or suspect)

diseases._note: Outbreak-only reportable; sporadic cases not reportable.

diseases.common_name: Spotted fever rickettsiosis (e.g., Rocky Mountain spotted fever)

diseases._note: Submit within one working day if pregnant (ADHS R9-6-202).

animal_reporting._note: Bovine TB (M. bovis) only; ADA leads on cattle/dairy surveillance.

diseases.common_name: Tuberculosis latent infection in a child 5 years of age or younger
Viral hemorrhagic fever (Ebola, Marburg, Lassa, etc.)

animal_reporting._note: Not formally reportable for animals, but ADHS encourages cross-species sentinel notification given AZ endemicity.

diseases._note: Although technically not on the AZ R9-6-202 explicit list, valley fever is reportable per separate provider obligation under R9-6-201; included for comprehensive AZ One Health coverage.

reportable_cases._description: Reportable disease cases placed on existing patients across the synthetic dataset. Each case is a FHIR Condition resource with the _reportable extension carrying reporting metadata. Counts are calibrated to be visually meaningful for the demo (modestly inflated above population-proportional rates), with county endemicity weighting where appropriate.
reportable_cases._caveat: Synthetic. All patient identifiers and case timing are synthetic. County-level endemicity weighting reflects published ADHS and CDC patterns but absolute counts are demo-calibrated, not epidemiologically projected.
